//counts: Measured 2026-10-10 with the AI scribe finished: 2182/1440/735/7 with NO database, and 2182/2177/0/5 against a local PostgreSQL 17.10. +28 over the 2026-10-05 figures. 19 of the 28 ALWAYS RUN: scribeInput (9 - the drafting request contract, including the rule the whole provider choice rests on, that two voices with nobody named is REFUSED rather than drafted from both); scribeContract (8 - the absence rule recalibrated, see below); errorHandler (2 - a deliberately-written 5xx sentence may reach the user while a plain 500 still may not, plus a closed-list grep over every place that sets the flag). The other 9 need a database - the consent gate in consultations.test.js: no microphone until somebody records that the patient was asked, the gate failing CLOSED cross-tenant AND on another patient in the same pharmacy, a finalised note having nothing left to transcribe, the FIRST confirmation being the one kept, no role gate on consent while finalising keeps its own, a recording on the record even when the draft is thrown away, two recordings being two events, the scribe writing nothing anywhere, and the structural invariant that NO table in the schema has a column that could hold a recording or a transcript. Those 9 move the SKIPPED ceiling 726 -> 735, declared here per the rule. FOUR DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY DRIVING THE REAL ENDPOINTS AND THE LIVE MODEL, all invisible to a green suite. (1) An unreachable transcription provider came back as a 500 with a masked message, telling a pharmacist nothing - least of all that the note has to be typed, which is the whole designed degradation. (2) THE SHARPEST: the absence rule refused a FAITHFUL draft. The patient said "No fever" and "No I do not smoke at all"; the model wrote "No fever. Did not smoke."; the old regex called it an invented negative. A pharmacist asks "any fever?" and the patient answers, so that is the NORMAL case and the rule would have refused nearly every honest draft while passing all 12 tests. It now asks whether the PATIENT SAID IT, which is possible only because the model sees just the patient’s turns - and is STRICTER where it matters, catching "Not diabetic" and "has never had tuberculosis", phrasings no list contained. (3) finishReason "length" with ZERO characters on every realistic transcript: this deployment’s model spends tokens reasoning and they never appear in content, so maxTokens 400 was consumed entirely by thinking - and the screen reported it as "the recording caught too little", a FALSE statement about the patient’s consultation. (4) An all-blank transcript claimed the recording was empty. Mutation testing: 23 mutations run across the contract, the gate, the absence rule and the client invariants. 22 turned the right test red; the 23rd - making a SUBJECTLESS negative ("None.", "Not recorded.") supported - left every test green, which is the allergy card’s "None" (0058) in the worst possible place, so a test was written and it then failed. Three of my own mutations were WRONG rather than the code, and retargeted. ONE existing test was AMENDED, not relaxed: consultationLayout’s class-is-defined invariant now reads ConsultationScribe.jsx too, because a second file renders inside this screen and leaving it out would silently exempt the newest ui- classes from the one test that checks a class name was kept. It caught a missing .ui-scribe-heard rule on its first run. The client suite is 340 across 28 files, all green.

//lastChange: The AI scribe, finished (2026-10-10). Three requests, not one: consent, then audio in / speaker-separated turns out with NOTHING drafted, then a draft once the pharmacist has said which voice is the patient. The middle step stops short on purpose - the one question a model must not answer is which voice IS the patient, because its answer lands in a clinical record as "the patient reported", so a person answers it in one tap. NOTHING in the feature writes to the note: the draft returns to the screen and is accepted through the ordinary PATCH, so the note has one writer and a draft nobody accepted leaves no trace - pinned structurally and mutation-checked. 0071 adds two consent columns and NOTHING that could hold a recording, which is how "we do not keep the audio" stays true without anybody maintaining it. Consent has no role gate (the person who asks the patient is whoever is standing in front of them, often a technician; requiring a pharmacist would mean the nearest person clicking it on their behalf, a worse record than the true one) while finalising keeps its own. The transcript is NOT stored server-side between the two requests, which is why the client sends it back: a row with a short lifetime is still a row. ALSO FIXED HERE, because the scribe depends on it: errorHandler masked every 5xx message, so a deliberately-written 503 sentence could not reach a user. `expose` is opt-in and nothing else sets it. That same masking means routes/pharmacies.js and routes/website.js have 503 wording that has never been seen by anybody - a real defect in two other features, found while tracing this one and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED here, because it belongs in a change about them. NOT VERIFIED: the screen was never clicked through (the dashboard needs a Supabase sign-in, which is the owner’s account), there is no microphone in this environment, and the two-voice Deepgram path is still unexercised against real audio because the free key has expired - which is how defect (1) above was found. The safety machinery is measured; the ergonomics are not. A KNOWN GAP left open: withinTranscript compares character counts, so it catches a long fabrication from a short recording and cannot catch a short one - "Reports cough and vomiting" from a transcript saying only "cough" passes. On the realistic case it measured 675 against 689. Closing it needs entity-level grounding and is its own work.
